name: ShelterBox: emergency shelter (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: by share of the result at the defaults, low-income conflict and displacement settings (Mozambique stand-in) about 78% and Asia and the Caribbean (Bangladesh stand-in) 22%, each spread over its countries by 2025 grants to partners (note 5 of the accounts; Ukraine and Malawi, under 0.2%, left out).
summary: ShelterBox, a UK disaster-relief charity, gave emergency shelter, household items and cash to more than 231,000 people in 17 countries and territories in 2025, about three fifths of them in conflict and displacement (Syria, Yemen, Cameroon, Chad, Somalia, Gaza) and the rest after disasters (Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica, typhoons in the Philippines, earthquakes in Myanmar and Afghanistan), spending 16.1 million pounds on the programme and 4.8 million on fundraising. This model values the shelter and items as consumption on the site's log scale at two stand-in places' consumption, and adds the few deaths and illnesses they avert. The result is about 0.3 years of healthy life per 1,000 dollars, above most relief models on the site because the aid goes to very poor people, where 46 dollars of goods a person counts for much. The biggest uncertainties are the poorest households' consumption and how much of the spending reaches people as goods; the effect on deaths and illness is our judgment, so the model is discounted by the shared missing-data slider.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Cost of the modelled program, including overhead
People supported with shelter and other essential aid in 2025

source.title: ShelterBox Annual Report 2025 (trustees' report and audited consolidated financial statements, year to 31 December 2025)
source.quote: More than 231,000 people were supported with shelter and other essential aid in 2025.

rows.explainer: ShelterBox's own count for 2025, in 17 countries and territories (Syria, Lebanon, Afghanistan, Palestine, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Sudan, Yemen, Myanmar, Jamaica, Chad, the Philippines, Ethiopia, Cameroon, Somalia, Mozambique), people reached by partners it funds included. Not independently measured: the doubt is in the delivery row. The 2024 report counted 277,820 people for 22.6m pounds, a similar cost per person.

rows.label: Cost per person reached
rows.explainer: Context: about 120 dollars a person, or roughly 600 dollars a family of five, all costs included.

rows.label: Death rate among the people reached over the months the aid covers, without the response
rows.explainer: ShelterBox's 2025 work was split between protracted conflict and displacement (Sudanese refugees in Chad, displaced families in Somalia, Yemen, Syria, Gaza, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Ethiopia) and sudden-onset disasters (Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica, typhoons and an earthquake in the Philippines, earthquakes in Myanmar and Afghanistan, floods in Pakistan) (annual report pp. 5, 10-13, grants note 5). After sudden-onset disasters death rates rise only modestly above normal once the first days pass (our American Red Cross and Americares relief models take about 0.012); in camps and conflict zones they reach Sphere's emergency threshold of 1 per 10,000 a day (0.0365 a year; our MSF relief model takes 0.055 for newly displaced people). With about three fifths of the grants going to conflict and displacement, many of them protracted rather than new, our judgment is 0.016, from 0.009 to 0.04.

rows.label: Death rate in the same population before the crisis
rows.explainer: Crude death rates in the countries served (UN World Population Prospects via the World Bank): about 6 per 1,000 a year in Sudan, Syria, Yemen and the Philippines (facts/sudan.json 0.0063), 8 to 10 in Myanmar, Somalia, Chad, Cameroon and Burkina Faso (facts/drc.json 0.0084 and facts/south_sudan.json 0.0098 as neighbours). Weighted towards the African and Middle Eastern responses, 0.008, from 0.006 to 0.01.

rows.label: Share of the excess deaths the shelter and household items avert among the people reached
rows.explainer: No study measures what emergency shelter or household items do to mortality: the evidence synthesis of shelter self-recovery programmes (Maynard, Parker and Twigg 2017, Humanitarian Evidence Programme, https://fic.tufts.edu/wp-content/uploads/Shelter-Executive-Summary.pdf, p. ii) rates the evidence on physical and mental health 'Inconsistent Small (2) Limited'. Shelter, blankets and stoves protect against exposure in winter (Afghanistan, Syria, Gaza), mosquito nets in some kits against malaria (Chad, Cameroon, Burkina Faso), water carriers and hygiene items against diarrhoea. Anchors on the site: our MSF relief model takes 0.75% (0-2%) for items other than nets and adds nets separately; our American Red Cross relief model takes 3% (0-10%) for cash and relief items. Shelter is the item most tied to exposure, and some kits carry nets, so our judgment is 2%, from 0.3% to 6%.

rows.label: Years of the crisis the aid covers per person
rows.explainer: A tent or tarpaulin shelter lasts months in use (ShelterBox's tent life-cycle study, annual report p. 17, assumes a 12-month lifespan); household items about as long; mudbrick and durable shelters longer, but excess mortality fades within months as other aid arrives. Our judgment, half a year, from three months to a year.

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the years covered, times the share the response averts.

rows.label: Share of the deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: Excess deaths in displacement and after disasters fall most on young children and the old; in camps and famines 40-60% are under five, after sudden-onset disasters in middle-income countries fewer (our American Red Cross relief model takes 30%). With about three fifths of the work in low-income conflict settings, our judgment is 40%, from 25% to 55%.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at five or older, share aged 5 to 14
rows.explainer: Older children have the lowest death rates of any age; in the young populations of Chad, Somalia and Yemen they are a larger share than in middle-income settings (the Red Cross model's 10%). Our judgment, 12%, from 5% to 20%.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
rows.explainer: Working-age adults are a large share of young low-income populations and die from injuries in clean-up; the old die more of exposure. Our judgment, 40%, from 25% to 50%; the rest are valued at the 50-74 band.

rows.label: Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life.

rows.label: Episodes of acute illness averted per person reached
rows.explainer: Mosquito nets in some kits avert malaria episodes, water carriers, filters and hygiene items diarrhoea (water treatment and hygiene cut diarrhoea by about 30%, Wolf et al. 2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/s0140-6736(22)00937-0), shelter and blankets respiratory illness in cold seasons. With nets and hygiene items in a minority of kits and a few episodes a person a year in crises, our judgment is 0.04 episodes averted per person, from none to 0.12 (our MSF relief model takes 0.06 for kits richer in nets and hygiene items).

rows.label: Length of an episode of acute illness
rows.explainer: Malaria, diarrhoea and respiratory episodes last about five days when treated or self-limiting (GBD's moderate acute episodes last about a week): five days, from three to eleven, as our MSF relief model.

rows.label: Share of the episodes averted that are diarrhoea
rows.explainer: Our judgment: about two fifths diarrhoea (water carriers, filters, hygiene items), the rest malaria and respiratory infections (nets, shelter, blankets).

rows.label: Illness averted per person reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Episodes averted × their length × GBD's disability weights for moderate diarrhoea and a moderate acute infection, mixed.

rows.label: Other direct costs of charitable activities, 2025 (pounds)

source.title: ShelterBox Annual Report 2025 (trustees' report and audited consolidated financial statements, year to 31 December 2025)
source.quote: Expenditure on charitable activities Staff costs 2025 £000 2,885 Grants 2025 £000 7,183 Other attributable costs 2025 £000 5,169

rows.explainer: Aid items drawn from stock (stock fell from 4.929m to 3.614m pounds over the year, balance sheet p. 47), freight, warehousing, travel and other direct costs of the responses, gifts in kind included.

rows.label: Share of grants and direct costs that reaches people as shelter, items, materials or cash
rows.explainer: Partners' grant budgets and ShelterBox's direct costs both include staff, transport and offices besides what people receive; freight to the place is part of an item's local value, so it counts. Anchors: the IFRC appeals in our American Red Cross relief model spent 68-97% on the sectors that reach people; that model takes 65% of the grants as reaching people. Our judgment, 65%, from 50% to 80%.

rows.label: Shelter, items and cash delivered per person in the year (US$)
rows.explainer: The value of what people received, at what it cost to get it to them (in-kind gifts included), over the people reached: about 46 dollars a person at the best guesses. Shelter and items are valued as consumption on the site's log scale; their effect on deaths and illness is counted above as well, a small share of the total and a different good (survival, not the shelter's use).

rows.label: US prices in 2017 relative to 2025
rows.explainer: Puts 2025 dollars of aid into 2017 prices, the year of the PPP factors; it applies to the baselines too (with their own year), so it nearly cancels in the log gains.

rows.label: US prices in 2017 relative to 2024
rows.explainer: Puts the 2024 consumption figures into 2017 prices for the baselines.

rows.label: Crisis-affected households' consumption per person, as a share of their country's survey mean
rows.explainer: Displaced and disaster-affected households consume well below their country's mean over the year. Anchors from the World Bank's Poverty and Inequality Platform, as in our American Red Cross relief model (same row, same value): the poorest 40%'s mean is 0.33 of the survey mean in Mozambique, 0.54 in Bangladesh and 0.55 in Myanmar. Relief targets the poorest and worst-affected, about the poorest 40%. Our judgment, 0.42, from 0.28 to 0.7.

rows.label: Share of the people reached in low-income conflict and displacement settings (valued at the Mozambique stand-in)
rows.explainer: The grants (note 5, p. 54) went 4.783m of 7.183m pounds (67%) to partners in Africa (Chad, Cameroon, Somalia, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Malawi: 2.777m), the Middle East (Syria, Yemen, Gaza: 1.999m) and Ukraine (7k), and 2.400m to Asia and the Caribbean (Philippines, Myanmar, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Jamaica). ShelterBox's own deliveries from its warehouses in Barbados, Cebu and Pakistan went mostly to Jamaica, the Philippines and Pakistan, so the people are less weighted to Africa and the Middle East than the grants. Our judgment, 62%, from 50% to 75%. These people are valued at Mozambique's consumption (486 dollars a person, close to Chad's, Somalia's, Yemen's and Syria's), the rest at Bangladesh's (a middle stand-in between Myanmar and Afghanistan below and the Philippines and Jamaica above).

rows.label: Consumption per person of the people reached in low-income settings (2017 PPP $), Mozambique stand-in
rows.explainer: Mozambique's household consumption per person (World Bank, 2024 dollars) on the household survey's scale (the shared ratio), at the affected households' share, in 2017 prices and PPP.

rows.label: Consumption per person of the people reached in Asia and the Caribbean (2017 PPP $), Bangladesh stand-in
rows.explainer: Bangladesh's household consumption per person on the survey scale, at the affected households' share, in 2017 prices and PPP.

rows.label: PPP conversion (2017 international $ per US $), weighted
rows.explainer: The two stand-in countries' shared PPP facts, weighted by the people; the log gains use each country's own.

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of the people reached (PPP), weighted
rows.explainer: The two baselines weighted by the people, for reading; the log gain is taken for each stand-in.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person, low-income settings
rows.explainer: A year's aid at the Mozambique stand-in's consumption.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person, Asia and the Caribbean
rows.explainer: A year's aid at the Bangladesh stand-in's consumption.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person
rows.explainer: Each stand-in's log gain at its own consumption, weighted by the people.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: Most of the value is the goods at their cost, which needs no effect study, but people value aid in kind below its cost when it isn't what they would have bought (in-kind vs cash comparisons find in-kind transfers worth somewhat less to recipients; ShelterBox's post-distribution surveys report high satisfaction, e.g. 93-100% in Pakistan in 2024); the deaths and illness rows are judgments anchored on other relief, not measured. Our judgment, 0.85, from 0.65 to 1 (our American Red Cross relief model takes 0.95 for cash and goods, our Americares emergency model 0.8 with more health care in it).

rows.label: Share of the outcome other responders wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: OCHA's Financial Tracking Service shows the 2025 shelter clusters of the response plans where ShelterBox worked funded at 13.4% in Somalia ($8.1M of $60.8M, plan 1221), 19.0% in Burkina Faso ($9.1M of $48.2M, plan 1259), 14.4% in Yemen ($24.5M of $170.0M, plan 1262), 17.9% in Afghanistan ($32.1M of $179.1M, plan 1263), 15.2% in Cameroon ($3.4M of $22.1M, plan 1266) and 26.7% in Syria (shelter, $47.1M of $176.5M, plan 1276; https://api.hpc.tools/v1/public/fts/flow?planId=1221&groupby=cluster and the same for each plan, retrieved 2026-11-14). So others met under a fifth of planned shelter needs, and ShelterBox's partners work where the clusters have gaps; after Hurricane Melissa and the Philippine typhoons, governments and many other agencies responded too. 1 - 0.2 = 0.8, times about 0.9 for responders outside the appeals (host communities, governments, diaspora) and the better-covered sudden-onset responses: our judgment, 70%, from 50% to 85% (our MSF relief model takes 72%).

rows.label: ShelterBox's own spending as a share of its programme's resources, gifts in kind included
rows.explainer: Donated stock and freight are others' resources behind the same aid (Convention 2).

rows.label: ShelterBox's share of the resources behind the aid, beyond gifts in kind
rows.explainer: Partners' own staff time and overheads beyond the grants, Rotary members and other volunteers who assess, pack and distribute (unpaid, 'hundreds' of volunteers, annual report p. 28), UNHCR in Chad and Food for the Poor in Jamaica co-delivering. The grants pay most of the partners' costs. Our judgment, 92%, from 80% to 100%.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: ShelterBox's cash share of its programme's resources times its share beside partners and volunteers.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity, compliance, follow-through)
rows.explainer: People counted as supported who got little (a single item), items sold or lost in further displacement, double counting across responses. ShelterBox runs post-distribution monitoring in its project cycle (annual report p. 14), but over half of its spending goes through partners in insecure places (Syria, Yemen, Somalia, Chad, Cameroon), where losses and counting errors are likelier than in our Americares and Red Cross relief models' disaster responses (90%). Our judgment, 85%, from 70% to 100%, as our MSF relief model for distributions to displaced people.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Others' fill-in is in the counterfactual; ShelterBox took 2.8m pounds of grants from institutions, corporations and trusts (16% of income, note 2) and says it receives 'extremely low levels of institutional funding' (p. 34), so little public money is displaced or drawn in. Our judgment, 1.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin (templates.md Convention 12): ShelterBox counts the people, but the value per person rests on our judged goods share, and the effect on deaths and illness is judged with no study of shelter against none, so the branch reads the shared missing-data slider.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Durable and mudbrick shelters lasting beyond the year, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Part of the work builds shelters that last years (in Somalia 200 durable and 130 mudbrick shelters, p. 13; mudbrick homes in Chad, p. 10; pakka houses in Pakistan in 2024), while the goods are counted as one year's consumption. Our judgment: a tenth of the value in shelters that give about another year and a half of use, discounted, 6% of the modelled value, from 0 to 15%.

rows.label: Preparedness, training and tenancy support, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Pre-positioned stock that speeds later responses (Jamaica from the Barbados warehouse, p. 15), community training on building back safer (Philippines, p. 11), tenancy agreements that protect displaced families from eviction (Somalia, p. 13), local jobs in clearing debris and building. Our judgment, 4%, from 0 to 10%.

rows.label: Harms not modelled (funging, crowding out local markets, emissions), as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Restricted gifts that let ShelterBox move unrestricted money elsewhere (all its work is the same kind, so little), items crowding out local traders, and the emissions of tents and freight (a tent's footprint is about 385 kg of CO2e, p. 17; at the site's deaths per tonne this is well under 1% of a family's value). Our judgment, -2%, from -6% to 0.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: The three shares above, summed with their signs.
